issues.legal_issue: The permission for a defendant to contest the adequacy of court fees in a civil suit does not itself authorize the defendant to seek revision of the court’s decision on that issue.
material_facts: The plaintiff filed a suit and paid court fees on the plaint.
The defendant objected to the valuation and adequacy of the court fees, and the trial court decided the issue after considering the valuation evidence.
The defendant sought revision of the court-fee determination.
issues.conclusion: The defendant could raise the court-fee issue before the trial court and assist it in deciding the issue, but the relevant provision did not confer a right to seek revision of that decision.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(2) of the Madras Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955 enables a defendant to plead that the suit is improperly valued or that the fee paid is insufficient, so that the court can decide the issue before evidence on the merits is recorded. It does not authorize a revision application by the defendant. Section 19 permits the court to conduct an inquiry, including by commission, into valuation and fee sufficiency; it does not give the defendant a revisional right. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.civil_suit_involving_plaint_court_fee: A plaintiff brought a civil suit in which the court had to determine the fee payable on the plaint.
predicates.defendant_raised_fee_objection: The defendant objected to the valuation of the suit or the sufficiency of the fee paid.
predicates.defendant_sought_revision_of_fee_decisio: The defendant asked a superior court to revise the court’s decision on the fee payable.

issues.definition: When a defendant raises a fee objection in a civil suit and then seeks revision of the fee decision, the permission to raise the objection does not itself authorize that revision.

issues.legal_issue: A defendant may not invoke revisional jurisdiction to challenge a court-fee determination when the challenge does not involve a ground within the revisional court’s jurisdiction.
material_facts: The defendant sought revision of the trial court’s determination of the court fees payable on the plaint.
The revision concerned the adequacy of the fee, and no question of jurisdiction was involved.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in entertaining the defendant’s revision application because no question of jurisdiction was involved.
issues.legal_principle: Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure confines revisional jurisdiction to the grounds set out in clauses (a) to (c), including a subordinate court’s refusal to exercise jurisdiction vested in it, assumption of jurisdiction it does not possess, or illegal or materially irregular exercise of its jurisdiction. A defendant who disputes the fee paid on a plaint has no right to seek revision merely on that basis. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.civil_suit_involving_plaint_court_fee: A plaintiff brought a civil suit in which the court had to determine the fee payable on the plaint.
predicates.defendant_sought_revision_of_fee_decisio: The defendant asked a superior court to revise the court’s decision on the fee payable.
predicates.no_revisionable_jurisdiction_issue_was_i: The defendant’s challenge to the fee decision did not involve a qualifying issue about the subordinate court’s jurisdiction or its exercise of jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a defendant seeks revision of a court-fee decision in a civil suit and the challenge involves no revisionable jurisdiction issue, the revision must not be entertained.
